claims.text: CrFeCoNiX alloys with X = Si, Mn, or Al can be considered in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
During oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C, formation of a stable, coherent protective oxide on CrFeCoNiX is governed by the alloy's configurational entropy.
Configurational entropy of the metallic alloy influences the thermodynamic stability of its oxide layer.
Greater oxide-layer thermodynamic stability leads to formation and persistence of a coherent protective layer rather than cracking or spallation.
CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys exposed above 900 °C are predicted to form a stable, coherent protective oxide layer.
Al-containing alloys can form protective Al2O3 that is more stable and slower growing than chromium oxide at high temperature.
CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys are expected to produce a more stable or coherent protective oxide than conventional alloys lacking high configurational entropy.
The hypothesis applies to oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C.
The hypothesis is bounded out below 900 °C and in non-oxidative or non-corrosive atmospheres.
Alloy composition and microstructure can influence protective oxide formation.
Surface preparation can influence protective oxide formation.
Across CrFeCoNiX alloys with different configurational entropies, oxide thickness and composition should correlate with configurational entropy.
Absence of a correlation between configurational entropy and oxide thickness or composition would falsify the proposed mechanism.
